answer.rationale: With the primary contract expiring in 14 days and the line already at 94% of committed volume with no buffer, switching primary vendor now carries unacceptable delivery risk per memory_c2's explicit warning about SLA misses from the low-cost alternative. Deferring is not viable given the hard 14-day expiration and no-auto-renew clause. Renewing outright leaves the 18% spend-cut mandate unaddressed. Negotiating terms with the incumbent (supported by memory_c4's margin recovery and memory_c6's volume-pricing precedent) offers the best path to meet the cost mandate while preserving the stability documented in memory_c1, without introducing a new, unproven supply relationship under time pressure. I verify memory_c2 to confirm the severity and consistency of the SLA-failure record before ruling out vendor switching, and memory_c4 to confirm the negotiation lever actually produced durable terms rather than a one-time concession, since the current spend-cut requirement is larger and more urgent than the prior case.
